name: What if the toilet is under a window?

mainEntity.name: What if the toilet ends up under a window in the new bathroom layout?
mainEntity.text: What if the toilet ends up under a window in the new bathroom layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: A toilet beneath a window is not automatically wrong, but it should be treated carefully in the layout plan. The main question is whether the window height, sill depth, and surrounding walls allow enough clearance and privacy. In some bathrooms, the window placement forces the toilet into the only available spot, but that does not mean it is the best final solution. If the toilet under a window creates a tight fit or makes it difficult to open and clean the window, consider shifting another fixture instead. A designer should evaluate whether the wall can support a different arrangement or whether a smaller window treatment, privacy glass, or alternate fixture placement would work better. The goal is to avoid a layout that feels compromised every day.
acceptedAnswer.description: A toilet under a window can work if the clearance, height, and privacy are acceptable, but it often creates design and practical issues. The main concerns are the window trim, privacy, ventilation, and whether the toilet location still feels comfortable to use.
